organizations.canonical_name: United States Army Air Forces, Ninth Air Force
organizations.active_dates: activated in 1942; documented for Couch in 1942-1943
organizations.normalization_notes: The 1944 interview's historical wording is preserved. During the documented period the Ninth Air Force was part of the United States Army Air Forces; it is not silently replaced by a modern successor.
The historical employer remains distinct from later successor entities and brands.

affiliations.date_precision: The interview gives Army entry as 21 June 1942, names the Ninth Air Force as the outfit, and gives OSS entry as May 1943. Exact transfer day and unit below numbered-air-force level are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The interview directly supplies the Army-to-Ninth-Air-Force-to-OSS sequence. It is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

affiliations.date_precision: In the same interview sequence, Couch identifies Sears, Roebuck when asked what he did in civilian life, immediately after dating Army entry to 1942. The exact hiring and separation dates and workplace are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: The direct personnel interview identifies the civilian employer and role. It is kept separate from the intervening Ninth Air Force assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed James B Cotton has a confirmed match to the exact private identifier and exact name in the official Army merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed identifier selects the matching Army row and dates Army entry to 28 September 1942 as a private in the Signal Corps.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact private identifier and exact indexed name establish the match despite another same-name Army row with a different identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry but does not identify an OSS start, a civilian employer or the Army-to-OSS sequence.
claims.match_notes: The full private identifier remains private. Civilian occupation value 422 is not published because no verified official label was established.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Elec A Couch is confirmed as Elec A. Couch Jr., an Army technical sergeant interviewed by an OSS review board in Cairo.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Couch, Elec A., Jr., T Sgt
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS interview prints the exact name, suffix, rank and same private identifier as the index; the official Army file independently contains the identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier across the index, OSS interview and Army file is conclusive. The interview restores the full name damaged in the merged-file transcription.
claims.temporal_assessment: The interview dates Army entry to 21 June 1942 and OSS entry to May 1943; the merged file instead dates Army entry to 22 July 1942.
claims.match_notes: The full private identifier remains private. The one-month Army-entry-date disagreement is preserved for archival review and does not undermine the exact-identifier match.

claims.claim_text: Elec A. Couch Jr.'s best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation is the Ninth Air Force, an intervening military assignment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Into what outfit? Ninth Air Force. When did you come into OSS? May 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS board's sequential questions place Couch in the Ninth Air Force after Army entry in 1942 and before OSS entry in May 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The interview's exact private identifier matches the index record.
claims.temporal_assessment: The direct sequence is strongly date-bounded, although the exact transfer day and subordinate unit are not stated.
claims.match_notes: This is classified as a military assignment and is not counted as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Elec A. Couch Jr.'s best-supported last civilian employer before Army service was Sears, Roebuck, where he was an auditor and trainee.
claims.evidence_excerpt: What did you do in civilian life? Auditor and trainee for Sears, Roebuck.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: In the same direct personnel interview that dates Army entry, Couch names Sears, Roebuck and describes his civilian role as auditor and trainee.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The interview's exact private identifier matches the index record.
claims.temporal_assessment: The chronology is strongly date-bounded to civilian life before Army entry in 1942, but exact employment dates are not stated.
claims.match_notes: The historical employer wording is preserved. No workplace, division or exact separation date is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Panagiotis D Coucoulis has a high-confidence match to the corporal assigned to communications in the OSS Athens personnel list of 1 January 1945.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Coucoulis, Panagiotis, D., Cpl. Communications Athens
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The visually inspected OSS list gives the rare exact full name and middle initial, corporal grade, communications duty and Athens location.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare exact name, middle initial and direct OSS personnel context provide a high-confidence match without requiring a namesake biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The document establishes OSS service as of 1 January 1945 but does not identify any pre-OSS employer or affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The entry is unmarked by the list's symbol for non-American-citizen Greeks. No nationality beyond that document convention is inferred.
